neighbours.label: the slot just before 'the least/best/most' in fixed idioms (to say the least, hope for the best, make the most of)
fire: The hotel room was disappointing, to say the least, so we left a day early.
Her first week at the new job was hectic, to say the least.
The weather looked grim, but the climbers set off and hoped for the best.
With no map and no signal, we could only hope for the best.
The students made the most of their one free afternoon in Lisbon.
He wants to make the most of his retirement by travelling widely.
Critics called the ending strange, to say the least, but audiences loved it.
The doctors had done all they could, and the family hoped for the best.
quiet: The hotel room was disappointing, to be honest, so we left a day early.
Her first week at the new job was hectic and full of meetings.
The weather looked grim, but the climbers set off before sunrise.
With no map and no signal, we followed the river downhill.
The students made a model of the solar system for the fair.
He wants to make a cabinet for his workshop out of old oak.
Critics called the ending strange, though audiences loved it.
The doctors had done all they could, and the family waited outside.
